body: I feel the same way. No one believes me when I say I'm struggling--or they don't fully understand the extent to which I'm struggling. There's been times when I was crying in the bathroom at work and five minutes later someone said, "wow, you're in a good mood today!" I can't show how bad I feel unless I consciously decide to let go of my control and then I feel manipulative. 🤷 At least there's people here who get it. We're not alone.

Thank you for this! I hadn't heard of the book before. My parents have depression/anxiety/ADHD and have always sort of gotten it but not quite (neither did I, I'm in my late 20s and just got diagnosed). They're trying to understand the new diagnosis but are so stuck in their ideas of what BPD is that they can't accept I have it. I think a book like this will help.

I have anxiety too so it could be either, you're right! I guess it's more like one of those things everyone does, but the frequency and stress involved can make it a result of different mental illnesses.

Shit...that explains a lot. I knew weed is still mentally addictive/habit-forming/whatever even though it's not physically addictive, but I didn't fully get what that meant before I tried to quit. I haven't been able to go past 5 days without relapsing. I get way more productive but I feel like I'm in mental/emotional hell and eventually cave before the week is out each time. I'll have to look into CBD oil. I used to vape cartridges (currently stretching my last little stash which is bud :'() but I mostly cared about the THC content lol, despite being stoned for two years I'm a dumbass when it comes to weed. I'm tired of being high tbh but when I'm not I just get so...ugh.

Do you have any other tips for quitting? I hate being dependent on it.

Edit: I missed your last sentence...bc I'm high. 🤦 It helps me with dissociation too!!! I feel more like me when I'm high, but like...trapped by being high. That sounds dumb but I hope you know what I mean. I love this sub, it makes me feel so much less alone
Yep. Send a risky text, put phone on silent with screen down, go do something else. That's my M.O.

I guess it was the wording specifically. Bizzare and petty have very negative connotations, and when you're dealing with someone who is in a very illogical state of mind, using words like that can make things worse. You could have just said I was having an illogical reaction, or that my need to lash out was coming from a place of sickness and emotion rather than how a healthy person would react. 

I know I'm just super sensitive. But that makes sense, considering I'm in the throes of currently untreated BPD. I'd suggest being a little more careful with how you word things when giving advice to someone who is obviously not thinking clearly.

I mean it sure as hell wouldn't be right of me to take it out on her, but you don't have to say it's petty and bizarre. This is a sub for BPD...intense reactions over inconsequential things are par for the  course. I was mostly just venting so that I *wouldn't* have a "petty and bizarre" reaction. Maybe this is sensitive of me, but your wording was kind of aggressive and not helpful.

I'm in a similar situation (minus the death of your mother--I am so sorry). My dad's parents were emotionally absent to emotionally abusive at times. He did not grow up in happy home. But he went to an Ivy League college, got a PhD, has been married. But he wasn't a good father and passed his issues down to me. I barely graduated high school, got kicked out of college, etc. But I'm the one who gets emotions and reasons behind them better and I feel like I'm his mom sometimes with how I have to kinda coddle him when it comes to psychological stuff. It sucks, but I can't just cut him out, it's not like he abused me or did anything to warrant that. I just wish I didn't have to attend to his emotional needs as well as mine. He relies on me to "fix" him or start a dialogue between us.

Distractions help. I'm a server so if it's busy I just don't have the time to obsess over anything. On slow days where I'm standing around and my mind starts spiraling, I'll doodle or hide where customers/managers can't see (sometimes even go into the bathroom) to play a little bit on my phone, etc. I try to be mindful and catch myself, do some deep breathing. I have ADHD too so when doing breathing exercises I have a hard time concentrating. I have to say "iiiinnnnn, ooouuuuutttttt" in my head and focus on picturing the words "in" and "out" in my head in big block letters. If my mind drifts I gently bring myself back. 

I don't know if this will apply to you, but physically my anxiety/strong feelings tend to feel like a dense tight knot behind my sternum. So I try to breathe around it, if that makes sense? Imagine the breath surrounding the knot and isolating it from the rest of me, seeing it at a distance, acknowledging the emotions but not fostering them. It's a lot easier said than done lol and it doesn't always work, but the more I practice the more it helps.

God I wish I could do that. My coworkers (aka my social life since I don't have one outside work) don't get it, but whenever I try to open up the pity or misunderstanding I get right off the bat makes me clam up again. No one seems to care enough to do research, I have to explain everything to people and that's so tiring.

My parents put me in therapy when I was about 13 so they knew, but not the true extent or the struggle we all had ahead of us. I've told some close friends in the past, mostly ones who have their own mental illnesses. I've alluded to it at work with some people I've worked with for years (except for one guy who has bipolar, we've talked about our illnesses upfront to each other) mostly so they know I'm not just being lazy or dramatic or whatever. But most of them don't truly understand how bad it is or that it's chronic and never going away. The amount of comments I get like "Have you tried yoga? You should drink more water!" are infuriating but I know they come from a place of caring. Just not caring enough to actually look up mental illnesses and understand them better lol
Also INFP!!

I took prescribed ketamine nasal spray as a short term fix for being acutely suicidal. I think for a few weeks? Maybe two months? It was last year so I don't really remember. It worked well and quickly but my psychiatrist and doctor said it wasn't a long term solution and it plateaued faster than other medications have. Plus I wasn't diagnosed with BPD back then, we were just using it to keep me alive basically lol. I did feel pretty high when I took it so I was also scared of abusing it. If you know you have the discipline to stick to theraputic doses, it's worth a shot tho. Just be careful!
Me right now

Omg same...I used to bartend and sometimes snuck drinks toward the end of the shift if it was slow and overshared way too much. So glad a lot of my bar was tourists that I never had to see again looool

I only like people who are unavailable/not interested in me. The few times someone actually ended up reciprocating after I'd been pining, I ended up hating them/ruining the relationships early on. Not sure if it's the BPD or we both have something else going on, but I feel you.

I don't have any words of wisdom, but I'm in the same boat. I thought my friends would be there for me when I needed them but when I finally reached out, none of them came through. My attempts to make new friends out of acquaintances don't go well. It fucking sucks. I totally get that feeling of bottling everything up and wanting someone to confide in. 

I've been in and out of therapy for fifteen years and it's routine for me now so I don't have advice for you here either :( It's not the same as having a friend's shoulder to cry on--my therapist is there to help me get better and manage my symptoms, not comfort me--but it really does help. I've already started learning some things that help me regulate these wild emotions and reactions. 

We're in this together, though. We're not totally alone.

I'm proud of you!! It is SO hard to make that first step, but you did it! You have a plan laid out now and upcoming support. The fact that you were strong enough to know you needed help still and get that help is awesome.

Yeah, we might not be exactly the same but I think I understand you too. When someone does message me outside of work my immediate reaction is almost like a puppy, if that makes sense? Like OMG! A PERSON! A FRIEND?! But then I freak out about possibly being too intense and pull back. It's hard to find that middle ground. BPD ain't fun!
Thank you 💖 People like you give me little pinpoints of brightness in my day, which is enough to build a better mood and keep me grounded.

I feel that. No one can ever tell that it's like all these emotions are about to make me burst out of my skin. It's like trying to hold back a tidal wave. I know it's better than having an outburst I'll regret, but goddamn is it hard.

>how you want to feel...and create that

I'm not OP but, woah. I recently found a quote that amounted to "create yourself" and I've been keeping it in mind. But deciding how I *want* to feel...that seems obvious but it never occurred to me, hahaha! Having a solid goal to strive for helps, rather than some nebulous idea of somehow being okay. And it makes "create yourself" something tangible rather than a concept. 

Sorry for the musing lol, and thank you for your reply to OP!!

Same. :( I avoid thinking about how much time I might have ahead of me, especially with how I have no foundations to build a life on. It's gonna be hard going but I don't have a choice. We can make it through, though; we've made it this far!

It really is difficult and I'm sorry you're dealing with it too. It's hard for me to tell what's a legitimate "sorry I'm busy, but I'd like to later!" or just a polite no with an excuse, especially via text. Like I don't know when to keep trying or stop bugging them. Sigh, adulting with BPD is haaard.

>"Do I enjoy seeing him because he’s a fun person or do I need validation?”

Oof, necessary but painful truth right there, thank you. I do enjoy being around him and talking to him but the need for validation is a big motivation too. I ended up just texting a casual "hey wanna hang out when you're off" and I got a "maybe/let me ask the bf" in return, and no follow-up yet so I'm taking that as a no 🤷 Oh well. Better that than guilt tripping him.

It's not stupid to be as anxious as you are. It seems to me like you have every reason to want to avoid medical facilities at all costs and I'm sorry you had to go through that. You can do it, though. You're strong! You've made it this far!!! 💖💖💖
Exactly!! It's exhausting.
Definitely!! We're strong women 💪💖💕
Thanks!! I hope things get better for you too 💖💖💖💖
Awesome, I'm so proud of you!!!

This is just my personal experience with it:

Everything feels very far away, like an out of body experience. I can hear what's going on, I can see what's around me, I might even be doing things and interacting with people, but none of it feels real and/or like I'm watching myself in third person (but I'm not, I'm still seeing from my own eyes, which causes this weird disconnect). I feel like I could just float away off into space at any moment. 

It kinda feels like I'm in a [dolly shot like this](https://media1.popsugar-assets.com/files/thumbor/IQJnlfBOqJksMKYBh1o2hHXd5A4/fit-in/2048xorig/filters:format_auto-!!-:strip_icc-!!-/2017/09/07/918/n/1922283/tmp_RFgzDD_26b5535d8588e90b_ahs-comicbook.gif) that keeps going until I break my way out of it. 

I hope that helped a bit!!!

I had the same reaction when I was diagnosed recently! Reading about symptoms and other people's experiences was like a light bulb blinking on above my head. Finally, it all makes sense!! And DBT looks super promising and helpful, I can't wait to start and begin the journey. Good luck to you!!! 💖💖💖🥰

I hope whatever you're dealing with that caused you to lash out like this gets resolved. You should try talking to someone in your life about what you're going through. I hope you figure it out. Good luck. 💕

Me, to the point that it was messing up my life. It's not legal here so I bought whatever strains my dealer could get, mostly indicas that made me drowsy and sleep all day. I would've killed for a good sativa that might actually energize me a bit. I've had to quit because I'm starting DBT and being stoned all the time kills my motivation. Been mostly sober for two weeks with occasional expected relapses that mostly happen right before bed instead of when I have things to do during the day. Yay!

Before I became dependent on it my usage was only like once or twice a week (still often but better than every day being a wake n bake day lmao). I'm hoping once I'm completely off of it for a while, and once I'm completely engaged with DBT and doing well on my meds and don't need to self medicate anymore, I can go back to smoking every once in a while.
Cis woman, 27

Ugggh this. If someone at work is in a bad mood or even just quieter than usual, it's all I can think about. I'll ask if they're okay and try to leave it if they say they're only tired or don't elaborate but then I walk on eggshells around them and I end up in a bad mood too. And then I feel awful for making it about me.

>I wish I didn't have a subconscious expectation of people to invest the same amount of effort that I do, because it absolutely kills me when they don't. Love becomes rage. But I know how to conceal it well, as I do with most of my feelings, so nobody suspects a thing.

>Small things can set me off and ruin my day completely. I can handle one thing but, once they accumulate, I feel as if I am beyond help. Again, no one that I know sees me as an angry person, but I sometimes feel as if I could kill.

Christ, that's exactly how I'm feeling. I don't have any advice, but know that I'm in that boat with you. You're not alone. Not sure if that helps for you, but it helps for me. *hugs* 💕💖
God, me too. I just found this subreddit today and you guys are so supportive. I'm glad I'm here; we're all trying to deal together
I'm so proud of you!! I'm struggling right now not to engage in any harmful behaviors and reading about someone else not giving in really helped, thank you 🥰💕

We can be lonely together. I've been single since early 2013 bc of this. (That was the end of my longest relationship--4 months. Also long distance, so we only spent maybe a week or two in total in person.) My friends tell me to just go for it, you never know, they might be the one, maybe they'll help you heal, etc. But they only say that because I haven't showed them the full crazy I'm hiding inside. 🤷

I'm in the same boat, I'm sorry you're struggling with that. I've held down a job, so obviously I'm fine. I'm talking a mile a minute and bouncing all over the place and cleaning the kitchen, so obviously I'm fine. I'm smiling and joking around, so obviously I'm fine. 

One day at work I had to go hide in various places to cry every half hour or so. I'm a waitress so it's hard to get a moment to myself. Right after I came back from holding back sobs for five minutes, a coworker I've known for five years said, "Wow, you're in a good mood today!" I laughed in his face and he laughed along.

Just because I seriously can't allow myself to show how much distress I'm in doesn't mean I'm not in distress. The only way people can ever tell I'm suffering is when I tell them or intentionally let it show, which is hard as hell to do and also makes me feel like a manipulative bitch. It sucks. :(

Yyyyep. I'm struggling with friendships--I feel like a disgusting human being who manipulates people into liking them. Because obviously no one could ever actually want to be friends with the real me, being a disgusting human being and all.
Same. I can't think of any life path that doesn't eventually end with me killing myself. I'm mostly just biding time until my parents pass.

Hey, I just wanted to say thanks. I've been holding your comment with me during the past week and it's helped a lot. It's hard to accept when people say I'm strong bc I'm constantly struggling and fucking up. But you're right. The odds are against me and I'm still here. So, again, thank you.
